description: Verify a rigged animated character mesh has its pivot at the FOOT (so state.position is the ground-contact point), not the geometric center. Catches animated GLBs that inherited a stale y_offset from a previous static (center-pivot) mesh — a pivot-convention mismatch that produces 0.5-1m floating.

params_schema.entity: entity_id_or_def — an animated character (typically has physics.body_type=character + a .glb model_3d)

framing.subject: character_feet_visible_against_ground
framing._doc: Same as no_floating — low height (0.3-0.6m), pitch slightly up. Frame the character's feet against the ground/horizon line.

prompt_template:
This low-angle capture frames the animated character {entity_label} at world {pos_entity}. The character is a RIGGED animated mesh whose pivot convention is FOOT-PIVOT (root bone at y=0). The engine sets the character's world Y to pos_entity[1] (typically 0 = ground).

Inspect: do the character's FEET touch the ground? Look at where the soles/foot bottom contact the ground plane.

Three possible failures:
  1. Floating — feet are visibly ABOVE ground (gap underneath). Stale y_offset from a prior pivot convention.
  2. Sunken — feet/legs visibly BELOW ground (legs partially through floor). Wrong y_offset OR pivot not actually at foot.
  3. Clean — feet flush with ground.

Answer:
  VERDICT: PASS | FAIL
  EVIDENCE: one sentence — describe the foot-ground relationship (gap above? sinking? clean?).
  CONFIDENCE: high | medium | low
common_fix: For animated rigged GLBs (Tripo3D animation pipeline ADR 0053): the FBX/GLB exporter places the root bone at the foot. Default y_offset MUST be 0 — do NOT inherit y_offset from a previous static center-pivot version of the same character. animate_smoke.py and the animation pipeline must pop legacy y_offset + y_offset_mesh BEFORE re-deriving (see [[feedback-reset-field-families-on-pivot-change]] for the empirical case). If the GLB has non-zero foot-bone Y in the file itself, that's a content-side fix in the animation prep.
